wv_air_space_boulder.blurb: Air Space Boulder is a slab-style boulder in the roadside zone of Coopers Rock State Forest in northern West Virginia, tucked just under the Warm Up Boulder. It holds 15 problems, all bouldering, and the bulk of them sit at V0, with a handful stepping up to V2, V3 and V4 and one problem below V0. That makes it friendly for newer boulderers and a handy stop for a warm-up round. The trail to it winds through the Kaleidoscope corridor, with the slab off to one side. Expect low-angle, technical movement rather than steep power.

wv_tier_2_boulders.blurb: Tier 2 is a cluster of boulders in the Moby Area of Coopers Rock State Forest, sitting just below the Moby Boulder itself. It has 15 bouldering problems covering a wide range, from an easy V0 up through a few V4 and V5 lines and a small number of much harder ones reaching V9 and V10, though most of the problems fall between V1 and V4. It is a well-loved stop with a crowded reputation on busy days, and it pairs well with the neighboring tiers for a full session of varied problems. Holds can be delicate, so it rewards careful footwork.

wv_first_wall_left.blurb: First Wall Left is the long, left-hand stretch of the First Wall near the Tilted Tree area of Coopers Rock State Forest in northern West Virginia. It carries 15 bouldering problems, mostly vertical faces and cracks with flat landings beneath them. The spread is wide: a couple of very easy lines and several V0 to V1 cracks, then a solid block of V4 to V6 problems, and a few much harder ones that reach V8 and V10. Walk down the gravel forest road to the climbers' trail and follow it downhill to reach the wall, which makes a good destination for strong climbers and crack fans alike.

wv_1_super_mario_boulder.blurb: Super Mario Boulder sits at the downstream end of Beauty Mountain in the New River Gorge, a short five to ten minute walk up the middle driveway and along the road. It has 15 routes, mostly sport with a few trad lines and top ropes. A couple of easy routes make it possible for beginners to get on the rock, but the real draw is the stack of hard lines: roughly a dozen climbs run from 5.10 into the 5.13 range. The setting is very shady, rarely busy, and the stone is high quality but can stay damp after a storm.

wv_4_promised_area.blurb: Promised Area is a small, seldom-visited crag in the Bridge Area of the New River Gorge, a quiet alternative when the main Bridge Buttress is packed. It holds 15 routes, mostly trad with a couple of sport lines, with grades from about 5.7 up to 5.12. Most of the climbs are in the 5.10 range, so it suits climbers comfortable on moderate gear routes, with a few easier lines and a handful of harder ones to grow into. Reach it by following the Bridge Buttress approach and then heading west on trails above the road.

wv_artist_point_area.blurb: Artist Point Area is a small bouldering spot in the Rocky Trail Eastside zone of Valley Falls State Park in northern West Virginia. A large, low overhanging boulder anchors the area, with smaller boulders beside it, and the main block can be seen from the trail after a short walk. There are 15 problems, all bouldering, with most falling between V1 and V4 and a few stepping up to V5 and V7. It is a good pick for a mixed-ability group wanting one of the best clusters of lines in the park.

wv_block_party_area.blurb: Block Party Area is a compact group of stacked, rectangular boulders within the Greenbrier Boulders of Coopers Rock State Forest, up the Furnace Road side of the forest in northern West Virginia. It holds 15 problems, nearly all bouldering plus one top rope. The grades are broad, from easy V0 problems to a few V6 and V7 lines, with a nice middle band around V3 to V5. The classics are packed close together, so you can link many problems in a short session without much walking between them.

wv_e_kaymoor_slabs.blurb: Kaymoor Slabs is section E of Endless Wall in the New River Gorge, found by continuing past Fern Point Cirque, where it is the first slab you meet. It has 14 routes, nine sport and five trad, spanning roughly 5.5 up to 5.13. Many climbers rate it as the best stretch of moderates on the wall, with a good number of 5.8 to 5.10 lines, while the upstream end holds the harder testpieces. Much of the cliff is taller than half of a 70 meter rope, so plan your rope management accordingly.
